title: Nearly Half of IMSS-Bienestar’s 12,750 Planned Clinics in 24 Mexican States Will Operate in January
author: Alma E. Muñoz and Néstor Jiménez
content:
_This article by[Alma E. Muñoz and Néstor
Jiménez](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Alma%20E.%20Mu%C3%B1oz) originally
appeared in the [November 24, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/11/24/politica/en-enero-
operaran-casi-la-mitad-de-los-12-mil-750-consultorios-del-imss-bienestar-
en-24-estados), Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City.** As the consolidation of health-sector institutions continues,
President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo reported that around **3,000 universal
health service clinics** have been established, out of a target of **12,750**
for the six-year presidential term in the 24 states affiliated with IMSS-
Bienestar. In January, 6,000 will begin operating.

To adapt the spaces where primary health care will be provided, 5,325
assemblies have been held, with the participation of nearly 200,000 people,
Well-being Secretary Leticia Ramírez reported.

At the morning press conference, she explained that the assemblies form
committees whose members become “guardians of health,” and funds are handed
over to the corresponding administrators to get the clinics running.

By early January, she said, we will have 6,710 clinics, and she specified that
3,292 Banco de Bienestar cards have been given to the committees “so that,
with the funds they already have, they can begin using them directly” for
painting, waterproofing, electrical and sanitary installations, ramps, guides
and perimeter walls, among other work.

Eduardo Clark García Dobarganes, undersecretary of Sectoral Integration and
Development at the Secretariat of Health, said the clinics will have 44
different items of equipment and standardized furnishings, from the desk and
the doctor’s or nurse’s computer to an examination table and mirror,
“everything they need not only for dignified care, but also for an identity
for the universal health service.”

He said applications remain open for health professionals to join.

> “To date, 82,000 people have registered and, as the assemblies progress, we
> have already begun the process of assigning doctors and nurses. To date,
> 4,310 people have already been assigned to a clinic.”
>
> Eduardo Clark García Dobarganes, Secretariat of Health

The president clarified that the clinics will have a doctor and a nurse with a
bachelor’s degree, along with a telephone assistance center and a mobile app
that will begin operating in January.

She emphasized that work continues in several areas of the health sector,
including strengthening IMSS, ISSSTE and IMSS-Bienestar “with more equipment,
permanent appointments, more staff and improvements in medicine distribution,
with the 120-day plan for the three institutions.”

## Progress on Consolidating the Health System in 120 Days

IMSS Director General Zoé Robledo highlighted, among the advances, that the
eight percent pay increase has been fully implemented. “It is received by 499
active employees and 370,000 retirees and pensioners.” He also said 11,325
people have received permanent appointments so far, “many of whom had
contracts to cover vacations and days off.”

This morning, it was reported remotely that positions would be awarded in
Tecámac, State of Mexico.

Robledo detailed that they are making progress on each of the 12 points they
must complete in 120 days.

Likewise, Alejandro Svarch, head of IMSS-Bienestar, explained the progress on
consolidation from the comprehensive renal health center inaugurated in
Toluca.

> On job security, “we are advancing the administrative validation processes
> so that more than 117,000 health workers have their positions. We will be on
> time for the payroll to be ready beginning December 15, and for all workers
> to be part of IMSS-Bienestar by January 1.”

He added that they continue to expand their care capacity with the addition of
more than 1,973 new health professionals.

He said delivery of 56 of the 195 pieces of high-tech equipment for rural
hospitals has been confirmed, and that, through the health routes, “13.3
million units of medicine have been distributed during this period.”

For his part, Martí Batres, head of ISSSTE, said they have reached 38.8
percent progress.
